summary: The note describes how technology startups are spreading beyond traditional tech hubs into smaller local economies, driven by affordable living, government incentives, universities, cloud tools, and remote work. It covers effects on traditional businesses, the workforce, sustainability, consumers, government infrastructure, and community culture, with dated examples. It closes with advice for existing businesses and notes challenges such as limited venture capital and high startup failure rates.
one_line: Technology startups are spreading into local economies, reshaping businesses, jobs, and communities, while facing challenges like limited venture capital and high failure rates.
key_facts: Since September 1, 2023, technology startups have been appearing in less traditional locations, with regions like Midwest's Silicon Prairie and the South's Silicon Hollar gaining traction.
Austin, Raleigh, and Denver combine affordable living, local government incentives, and major universities to attract startups.
On October 12, 2023, Maria Gonzalez of the Economic Development Institute observed that local governments have started to invest heavily in startup ecosystems for job creation.

A Dalton Economic Perspective study released November 5, 2023 found traditional retail saw a downturn in foot traffic as ecommerce startups rose, while IT support, legal services, and office space rentals saw spiking demand.
Office Innovations, a long-time office supply company, partnered with VR startup VirtualTech starting December 15, 2023, and began offering virtual office solutions.
Forward Pathways reported on January 8, 2024 that "job seekers who upskill now have the advantage in this shifting marketplace."
EcoTech, a clean energy software company, announced on February 14, 2024 that it had secured funding to expand its smart home energy solutions.
Bread & Butter bakery's sales reportedly increased by 30% after partnering with the app Foodie Finds on delivery, a partnership begun in March 2024.
The City of Boulder launched the TechStart Initiative on April 1, 2024, providing seed funding and office space to select startups.
The Chippewa Valley Code Fest took place on May 9, 2024, bringing together attendees from different backgrounds to celebrate innovation.
LearningTech Hub, founded on June 12, 2024, offers courses for business leaders and professionals to understand emerging technologies.
Challenges include limited access to venture capital outside major tech hubs, cyclical activity, and many startups failing within their first few years.
Cloud computing, open-source software, do-it-yourself tools, and pandemic-induced remote work have made launching startups more accessible and let talent be sourced globally.
